Mathematical Architecture & Formal Proof Routes

How the Lean formalization proves the theorems

The proof of Theorem A is organized around a single hub equivalence—linking the polyhedral condition (E-fin) to the module-theoretic condition (K₀-Hom)—from which the categorical, monoid-theoretic, polyhedral, infinite-dimensional, and geometric characterizations branch out. Where the paper cites external results that would be heavy to import (such as Cohn's universal skew field or King's polystable moduli theorem), Lean substitutes self-contained arguments.

Full technical route notes (PROOF-ROUTES.md) ↗ Statement-by-statement concordance ↗
Sections 1. Central bridge 2. Monoids, wide subcategories & polytopes 3. Generic modules & localizations 4. Geometry & rank two 5. Where Lean differs from the paper

1. The central bridge: (E-fin) ⇔ (K₀-Hom)

For a two-term projective complex U = (P−1 → P0) with cokernel C = H0(U) and Nakayama kernel N = ker(νu), Nakayama duality rewrites the Euler pairing as

⟨[U], [X]⟩ = dimk HomΛ(C, X) − dimk HomΛ(X, N).

When U is presilting and θ ∈ C°(U), the θ-semistable modules are precisely the objects of the τ-perpendicular category 𝒥(U) = C⊥ ∩ ⊥N, which is equivalent via Bongartz completion to mod ΓU for an algebra ΓU of rank n − r (PerpendicularReduction.lean, PerpendicularSimpleCount.lean). Separating the simple objects of 𝒥(U) by Bongartz summands proves that the dimension vectors of θ-stable bricks are linearly independent in K0(mod Λ) (StableSeparationWeights.lean).

  • Forward ((E-fin) ⇒ (K₀-Hom)): If nonzero modules M, N satisfy [M] = [N] and HomΛ(M, N) = 0, an inductive reduction extracts a nonempty finite semibrick with linearly dependent dimension vectors whose members are simultaneously stable at one integral weight θ (RationalExtraction.lean), contradicting linear independence at covered weights.
  • Converse ((K₀-Hom) ⇒ (E-fin)): At an integral class g = [P0] − [P−1] ∉ Σ(Λ), every differential p : P−1 → P0 admits a nonzero map coker p → ker(νp); an image B of minimal k-dimension is a brick stable at the corrected integral weight (dimk B) g − ⟨g, [B]⟩ [Λ] (MissingWeightWitnesses.lean). Over infinite fields, determinantal hypersurface avoidance produces infinitely many stable bricks at one weight and dimension vector; over a finite field 𝔽q, Frobenius orbit descent (AbsoluteFrobeniusCorrespondence.lean, SharpFiniteFieldCount.lean) produces, for each auxiliary extension degree s ≥ 1, at least qs/(c0 s) nonisomorphic ground bricks across a fixed finite set of weights with endolength ≤ dimk P0 and k-dimension ≤ s · dimk P0, yielding two nonisomorphic bricks of equal dimension vector stable at a single weight.

2. Grothendieck monoids, wide subcategories, and normalized polytopes

  • Grothendieck monoids & cancellativity (§4): Under (K₀-Hom), if X, Y ∈ 𝒯 have equal dimension vector, pushing out short exact sequences in 𝒯 along a nonzero morphism X → Y identifies their classes in M(𝒯) by induction on length (TorsionMonoidEmbedding.lean). Since K0(𝒯) ↪ K0(mod Λ) is injective for every torsion or torsion-free class (TorsionGrothendieckGroups.lean), injectivity of M(𝒯) → K0(mod Λ) is equivalent to cancellativity of M(𝒯), and contragredient duality transfers the criterion to torsion-free classes (MonoidCancellation.lean).
  • Wide subcategories as τ-perpendicular categories (§5.1): Under (E-fin), sim 𝒲 is a finite semibrick jointly stable at an integral weight; choosing a presilting cone C(U) of maximal dimension whose interior stabilizes sim 𝒲 forces 𝒲 = 𝒥(U), giving functorial finiteness (wide) and covers Filt(B) = 𝒯 ∩ (𝒯′)⊥ in f-tors Λ (WidePerpendicular.lean, BrickLabels.lean).
  • Normalized submodule polytopes (§5.2): Dividing projective Hom coordinates of submodules of a brick B by dimk EndΛ(B) places all vertices in {0, 1, …, endolength(B)}n (NormalizedPolytopes.lean), yielding (brick-discrete), (endo-stab), and the explicit bound 2(n − 1)(m + 1)n(n−1) for bricks of length ≤ m (SharpBrickGrowth.lean).

3. Generic modules, thick generation, and universal localizations

  • Excluding generic bricks by (Λ, Δ)-bimodule stability (§7.1): For a generic brick G with endomorphism division ring Δ, Δ-dimension defines a real stability weight; under (E-fin), a presilting representative places a nonzero Δ-subquotient into a large τ-perpendicular category Mod ΓU of smaller rank (GenericBrickExclusion.lean).
  • Two-term thick subcategories (§7.2): Over an E-finite algebra, any basic presilting complex U ∈ ℋ of maximum summand count generates the two-term thick subcategory ℋ ⊆ K[−1,0](proj Λ) via mapping-cone reduction, rational pencils, and Garcia's triangulated summand lemma (BoundedProjectiveHomotopy.lean).
  • Artin targets of Tor-vanishing epimorphisms (Corollary 7.9): Every universal localization Λ → Γ satisfies Tor1Λ(Γ, Γ) = 0 (LocalizationTor.lean). When Λ is E-infinite, a single projective map has a universal localization whose residual finite-dimensional quotient is still infinite-dimensional (ResidualLocalization.lean), which the descending chain condition forbids in any Artin algebra target (ArtinTargets.lean).

4. Geometry over k = k̄ and Stern–Brocot subdivision in rank two

Over an algebraically closed field, (E-fin) makes Jordan–Hölder multiplicities in 𝒥(U) unique at each dimension vector; degenerating semistable representations by scaling extension blocks shows both that King's projective moduli scheme ℳθss(Λ, d) has at most one closed point (KingModuli.lean) and that every semi-invariant weight space on every irreducible component of rep(Λ, d) is at most one-dimensional (Corollary C, ComponentMultiplicity.lean).

In rank n ≤ 2 over any field (Theorem B), each mixed-sign quadrant between ordered presilting boundary complexes (E, L) with Hom(E, L[1]) = 0 is subdivided at the mediant [Z] = [E] + [L]. Comparing Z with the cone of a nonzero morphism L → E[1] proves dimk Hom(Z, E[1]), dimk Hom(L, Z[1]) < dimk Hom(L, E[1]) (StableRigidComparison.lean), producing a finite cover of ℝ2 by compatible silting cones from which finiteness of bricks and τ-rigid modules is read off directly (RankTwoBricks.lean, RankTwoTauTilting.lean).

5. Summary of alternative proof routes in Lean

Result Manuscript argument Lean formalization route Primary modules
Prop. 7.6 (no-gen-grain) Uses Cohn's universal skew field of a free algebra to supply generic coefficients. Constructs a division ring directly from Malcev–Neumann well-ordered series on a bi-ordered finitely generated free group. DivisionRings/*, GenericGrainCriterion.lean
Thm. 7.8 (univ-loc) Deduces finite-dimensionality of universal localizations from (thick-gen). Also proves (E-fin) ⇒ (univ-loc) directly by rank induction via presilting-pencil inversion and Fitting decomposition. RigidPencilInversion.lean, UniversalLocalization.lean
Thm. 6.1 (moduli-pt) Cites King's bijection between closed points of ℳθss(Λ, d) and polystable modules. Splits extensions directly on vertex representations while preserving evaluation in AlgebraicGeometry.Proj. KingSplitting.lean, KingModuli.lean
Lem. 2.2 & Thm. 8.4 Uses τ-tilting cover counts for rank n − r, and cites DIJ/Asai for fan completeness ⇒ brick-finite. Proves s = n − r by dual spanning/independence inequalities, and bounds bricks in rank ≤ 2 directly from the finite sector cover. BongartzCounting.lean, RankTwoBricks.lean
